headline: Why is My New Paint Job Peeling So Soon?
articleBody: It's super frustrating when you invest in a fresh coat of paint, only to see it start peeling or flaking shortly after. Often, the culprit isn't the paint itself, but what happened (or didn't happen) before the paint even went on the walls. One major reason for premature peeling is inadequate surface preparation. If the walls weren't cleaned properly to remove dirt, grease, or old, loose paint, the new paint won't adhere well. Skipping necessary repairs like patching holes or cracks, or not sanding rough areas, can also lead to issues. Another common mistake is not using the right primer, especially on new drywall, stained surfaces, or when transitioning between very different paint types. Humidity and moisture can also play a role, so ensure any leaks or moisture problems are addressed first. For a whole-home project, getting a consistent, durable finish requires a lot of expertise and careful attention to detail.
